tasks.short: Resolve users' report and dashboard problems, explain results, and route defects for repair.

steps.what: Record the user's issue, affected report, symptoms, and urgency.
Reproduce the issue and inspect filters, permissions, refresh status, and underlying figures.
Search guidance and previous incidents for an explanation or workaround.

loop.input: Ticket text, read-only diagnostics, and guidance or resolved tickets the analyst may access.
loop.output: A cited draft explanation and workaround, or a clear no-answer result.
loop.check: Validate source references, report version, access scope, and prohibited instructions; the next step reviews the answer before sending.
loop.stop: At most two retrieval rounds and one draft; unsupported or conflicting answers go to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Users describe symptoms in varied language, and relevant explanations are spread across free-text guidance.

steps.what: Check the explanation and send instructions appropriate to the user's situation.
Record confirmed defects and agree the repair handoff with the maintenance owner.
Confirm the resolution with the user and close the ticket.

tasks.design: Configure structured intake in the {HELPDESK} and a read-only diagnostic panel covering the {BI} and {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded answer desk retrieves approved guidance from the {DOCS} and drafts cited replies; an analyst checks each reply before sending. Confirmed defects become linked maintenance records in the {PROJECT}, with repair status returned to the original ticket.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests lacked report versions, filter states, or reproducible symptoms. Guidance and earlier fixes were difficult to find across documents and tickets.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured forms and deterministic diagnostics remove repeated information gathering. Bounded retrieval and drafting make existing guidance easier to reuse without giving a model repair privileges.
tasks.still_hard: Unfamiliar failures, ambiguous numbers, and user misunderstandings still require investigation. Old tickets can contain incorrect advice or confidential details.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what the user was trying to decide, explain the result clearly, and recognise when a plausible workaround hides a deeper defect.

ambition.what: Guided first-use support for departmental budget holders

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time searching past tickets and more time resolving difficult cases and teaching users. They can recommend guidance improvements and defect priorities; access grants and production changes remain separately authorised.

reach.task: Help departmental managers interpret financial performance.
reach.learn: How managers use financial measures, common interpretation errors, and when accounting context changes the answer.

evidence.claim: Databricks documents analytical answers constrained by trusted assets and example queries. This supports the bounded-answer pattern, not arbitrary technical repair.
The Webmotors vendor case reports fewer manual analysis tickets. It is adjacent evidence, not a measured result for technical support in this design.
Spider 2.0 documents substantial difficulty with enterprise text-to-SQL workflows, supporting restricted diagnostics rather than unrestricted generated queries.
Structured intake, diagnostic checks, linked defect records, and cited draft replies are feasible building blocks. Savings and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: Users are internal staff, and diagnostic access follows their existing permissions.
Structured intake replaces missing-field chasing; unstructured requests can still be recorded manually.
Repair implementation is counted under maintenance, not again under this support task.
Drafting and diagnostic services cannot grant access, alter source records, or deploy changes.
The build starts with a small set of supported reports and approved guidance.
GDPR controls apply to ticket content and diagnostic data; EU AI Act literacy applies where relevant.
Build ranges include access and applicable national consultation effort; elapsed approval waits are not predicted.
unknowns: How many requests arrive through the shared queue versus personal messages?
Which diagnostic information can be collected through approved interfaces?
Is existing guidance accurate, versioned, and safe for retrieval?
How often do cases need live coaching rather than written instructions?
What retention and access restrictions apply to support tickets?
research_questions: Which recurring issues can be resolved with forms, direct guidance links, or deterministic checks alone?
Can a historical ticket benchmark distinguish helpful grounded replies from plausible wrong advice?
Which diagnostic fields reduce reproduction time without exposing unnecessary data?
new_work: Review draft answers and handle no-answer cases.
Retire stale guidance and redact unsuitable historical tickets.
Monitor retrieval failures and maintain the support benchmark.
Keep diagnostic connectors compatible with report changes.
Verify that linked repairs actually resolve the user's original problem.
tasks.statement: Provide technical support for existing reports, dashboards, or other tools.

tasks.short: Keep reporting templates, model documentation and reusable analysis assets current and easy to find.

steps.what: Locate new assets and update the library register.
Add descriptions and tags, and identify possible duplicates.

loop.input: Asset text, existing metadata and an approved tag vocabulary.
loop.output: Proposed descriptions and tags with supporting passages.
loop.check: Validate tags against the vocabulary and links against the register; the analyst checks descriptions and duplicate candidates.
loop.stop: One classification and one repair per asset; unreadable or ambiguous assets go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Hashes detect exact duplicates, but descriptions and topic tags require reading varied documents.

steps.what: Decide which assets remain valid and approve replacements.
Publish approved versions and archive superseded assets.
Notify affected users of changed templates and documentation.

tasks.design: Configure an asset register, version history, review dates and subscriptions in the {DOCS}. Use deterministic checks for missing metadata and exact duplicates, plus a bounded loop for proposed descriptions and tags; the {WORKFLOW} publishes or archives assets only after disposition approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Library upkeep competed with reporting deadlines. Inconsistent metadata made reusable assets hard to identify and assign for review.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document controls cover storage and versioning. Small metadata checks and bounded classification can now be built and maintained at lower cost.
tasks.still_hard: A document can look current while its assumptions are obsolete. Retirement also requires understanding which reports still depend on it.
tasks.human_edge: The BI lead judges whether an asset is analytically sound and safe to reuse in a different financial context.

ambition.what: Certified profitability templates for budget analysts

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time filing assets and answering location questions, and more time improving reusable methods. With delegated authority, they can approve routine metadata corrections; approval of analytical replacements stays with the BI lead.

reach.task: Reuse profitability templates in departmental planning.
reach.learn: Allocation methods, forecast assumptions and how template users interpret financial measures.

evidence.claim: Document libraries can provide metadata, versioning, review reminders and subscriptions through configuration.
Exact duplicate detection is deterministic; topic descriptions for varied prose can use a bounded classification loop.
Approval of analytical validity requires knowledge beyond document freshness and file similarity.

assumptions: The library mainly contains reporting assets, rather than executable production models needing separate deployment controls.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
The supplied mailbox share is treated as weak; change notices form a distinct but small part of upkeep.
Archiving preserves version history and follows the approved retention policy.
GDPR applies where assets include personal data. Access work includes inherited permissions and applicable national consultation requirements.
unknowns: Which repositories hold the assets?
Is there an existing register and reliable version history?
Who can approve retirement or replacement?
Which reports depend on each asset?
Which retention and access rules apply?
research_questions: Can the existing document library support the register without a separate application?
Which dependency references can be extracted deterministically?
Does a small tag vocabulary improve retrieval for adjacent finance roles?
new_work: Review proposed descriptions, tags and duplicate candidates.
Resolve assets without a reviewer or clear dependency record.
Maintain review dates, subscriptions and the tag vocabulary.
Check that archiving preserves required history and access controls.
tasks.statement: Maintain library of model documents, templates, or other reusable knowledge assets.

tasks.short: Monitor customers and prospects for financial exposure, growth opportunities and changes in demand.

steps.what: Extract customer, prospect, sales and receivables data.
Match customer identifiers and reconcile totals in a workbook.
Refresh customer segments, exposure measures and trend views.
Interpret unusual movements and propose monitoring priorities.
Agree priorities that affect financial exposure or commercial action.
Send approved priorities and dashboard links to relevant teams.

tasks.design: Configure scheduled transfers from the {CRM} and {ERP} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, with identifier matching and reconciliation checks. Refresh a certified customer dashboard in the {BI}, route exceptions through the {WORKFLOW}, and distribute priorities through the {EMAIL} after finance approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer identifiers, financial definitions and refresh schedules differed across sources. The workbook absorbed those differences without a maintained integration.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors and scheduled refresh handle much of the task. AI-assisted coding makes the remaining matching rules and reconciliation checks cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Prospect data is incomplete. A movement can reflect seasonality, a disputed invoice or a real change in demand.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst connects financial signals with market context and distinguishes useful opportunities from misleading correlations.
tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time assembling views and more time investigating exposure changes. With delegated limits, they can choose which customer cohorts need investigation; financial and commercial actions still require their existing decision makers.

reach.task: Prioritise customer exposure reviews.
reach.learn: Credit policy, ageing interpretation and the limits of aggregate customer signals.

evidence.claim: Scheduled refresh, identifier matching and total reconciliation can run deterministically.
Copilot in Power BI supports report creation over prepared semantic models; model preparation remains necessary.
Uber reports faster query writing, while also reporting invented tables; query assistance does not establish customer judgement.

assumptions: This finance role monitors customer profitability, receivables exposure and demand, rather than running outreach.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.
The structured-data prior supports deterministic processing; the low rule-coverage prior applies mainly to interpretation.
Existing supported connectors are assumed; custom source interfaces would increase integration effort.
GDPR applies to identifiable customer data. Access and consultation estimates include checking applicable national rules if employee-level data enters the dashboard.
unknowns: Which sources contain reliable customer identifiers and control totals?
Which measures are already certified?
What customer data may this role access and combine?
Who approves monitoring priorities and resulting actions?
Does the dashboard include individual staff performance?
research_questions: Can existing connectors and refresh settings replace the current exports?
Which reconciliation failures should stop a refresh rather than create a warning?
Which prospect signals have demonstrated value for financial monitoring?
new_work: Review unmatched customers and failed reconciliations.
Maintain identifier mappings and measure definitions.
Check refresh failures and access changes.
Review whether monitoring thresholds still identify useful cases.
tasks.statement: Identify or monitor current and potential customers, using business intelligence tools.

tasks.short: Create and review technical specifications so financial reports implement agreed data and measure definitions.

steps.what: Clarify reporting questions, definitions and acceptance criteria with the requester.
Inspect source fields, relationships and available financial measures.
Draft mappings, calculations, refresh requirements and report layout.
Check mappings and example calculations against financial control totals.
Review design trade-offs and approve the development baseline.
Publish the approved specification and link it to development work.

tasks.design: Capture agreed requirements in structured forms in the {WORKFLOW}, and read schemas and certified measures from the {DATA_PLATFORM} and {BI}. Generate the specification in the {DOCS}, run deterministic mapping and calculation checks, and link the approved baseline to the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements, schema details and calculation examples were maintained separately. Documentation drifted as designs changed.
tasks.enabler_now: Metadata interfaces and structured forms support a common specification record. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of generators and validation checks without needing a model to invent mappings.
tasks.still_hard: Financial definitions can conflict across teams. Performance, access restrictions and source limitations still require design trade-offs.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst resolves what a measure should mean and tests whether the proposed report answers the actual financial question.

ambition.what: Weekly resolution of conflicting report measures before development

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more of the week resolving definitions and testing report usefulness, with less repeated documentation. With delegated authority, they can select established measures and require unresolved definitions to be settled before development; new accounting interpretations still need finance approval.

reach.task: Translate accounting policies into report measures and reconciliation criteria.
reach.learn: Recognition rules, period cut-offs and how ledger controls constrain reporting definitions.

evidence.claim: Structured requirements and source metadata can populate technical documentation through deterministic templates.
Schema references, calculation examples and control totals can be checked with deterministic code.
Conflicting financial definitions and design trade-offs require accountable human decisions.

assumptions: Requirements are structured after the clarification conversation; unresolved mappings are left blank for human completion.
Generation handles established measure patterns and layouts, rather than inventing a complete design.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
The existing sources expose readable metadata; otherwise integration effort increases.
GDPR applies to sample data and access design. Consultation estimates include checking national rules where the report concerns employees.
unknowns: Are schemas, measures and requirements accessible through supported interfaces?
Which report patterns are stable enough to generate?
Who approves technical baselines and accounting definitions?
Which control totals and representative sample datasets are available?
Does the proposed report involve personal data or employee monitoring?
research_questions: What proportion of existing specifications follows repeatable patterns?
Can the generated specification preserve traceability when schemas change?
Which validation checks catch design defects before report development?
new_work: Complete unresolved mappings and review generated specifications.
Maintain structured requirement fields and document templates.
Update validation rules when measures or schemas change.
Handle failed checks and preserve approval history.
tasks.statement: Create or review technical design documentation to ensure the accurate development of reporting solutions.

tasks.short: Talk with industry contacts and turn their observations into useful financial and market context.

steps.what: Read recent industry material and prepare questions for contacts.

loop.input: Approved industry material, previous industry notes and research questions.
loop.output: A conversation brief with source-linked observations and proposed questions.
loop.check: Validate source references and dates; the analyst checks relevance and disclosure boundaries.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per brief; missing evidence stays marked unknown and falls back to manual preparation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise the brief, but varied prose needs reading to propose relevant questions.

steps.what: Agree a suitable time and agenda with the contact.
Discuss trends, test interpretations and ask follow-up questions.
Write up observations, sources and agreed follow-ups.

loop.input: Analyst-written industry notes and the conversation brief.
loop.output: A draft trend brief separating attributed observations, uncertainties and agreed follow-ups.
loop.check: Every substantive observation links to a note; the analyst checks attribution and confidential content.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous statements remain unresolved for manual editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes vary in structure and contain tentative statements that fixed fields cannot reliably extract.

steps.what: Assess credibility and approve implications for internal use.

tasks.design: Use templates in the {DOCS} and bounded drafting loops to prepare source-linked conversation briefs and organise analyst-written notes. Configure scheduling drafts in the {CALENDAR} and {EMAIL}; the analyst approves invitations, conducts conversations and approves the trend brief for internal use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful context was spread across prose and personal notes. Relationships and uncertain claims could not be handled through fixed rules alone.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded models can draft questions and organise notes, while existing scheduling features reduce coordination work.
tasks.still_hard: Contacts may withhold information or offer biased accounts. Trust, confidentiality and restrictions on sharing competitively sensitive information require human judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst builds trust, notices hesitation and asks questions that reveal the limits of a claim.
tasks.altitude: The analyst has more time for substantive conversations and comparison of conflicting accounts. They can select topics and contacts within an agreed research remit; authority to make external commitments does not change.

reach.task: Assess supplier concentration and resilience signals.
reach.learn: Evidence grading, scenario analysis and how to distinguish an early warning from an unsupported rumour.

evidence.claim: Templates, scheduling configuration and bounded summarisation can reduce preparation and paperwork.
Relationship-building and assessing a contact's credibility remain human work.
The EU AI Act includes AI literacy duties relevant to staff using these drafting loops.

assumptions: The task includes substantive conversations; their share exceeds the supplied meetings prior because that prior understates the task's defining activity.
Industry material and conversation notes contain free text, despite the strong structured-input prior.
The design uses analyst-written notes and does not depend on recording conversations.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to contact details and attributable notes. Access work includes permitted model processing and applicable national consultation rules.
unknowns: Which contacts and source materials may be used?
What information may be disclosed or retained?
Which internal audiences may receive attributed observations?
Who may approve invitations and external follow-ups?
Which employee consultation requirements apply to the proposed tools?
research_questions: Do source-linked briefs improve question quality in a small pilot?
Can note extraction preserve uncertainty and attribution without adding claims?
Which scheduling steps are already available through configuration?
new_work: Review generated questions and extracted observations.
Correct attribution, uncertainty and confidential details.
Maintain approved source lists and briefing templates.
Handle scheduling exceptions and track agreed follow-ups.
tasks.statement: Communicate with customers, competitors, suppliers, professional organizations, or others to stay abreast of industry or business trends.

tasks.short: Keep financial datasets, measures, dashboards, and reporting methods accurate and usable.

steps.what: Collect refresh failures, user defects, and requested reporting changes.
Inspect dependencies, source changes, and affected reports to diagnose the issue.
Agree changed measure definitions, priorities, and acceptance criteria.
Edit queries, measure definitions, mappings, and dashboard layouts in a development workspace.
Compare changed outputs with control totals, prior results, and access expectations.
Review test results and authorise deployment of the candidate release.
Update the measure catalogue, change record, and user guidance.

tasks.design: Configure a maintenance queue in the {HELPDESK} and dependency views in the {BI}; use parameterised definitions and reusable layouts for routine edits. Deterministic checks in the {DATA_PLATFORM} compare candidate releases with financial and access benchmarks before a BI lead approves deployment. Generate change records in the {DOCS} from the approved specification and release log.
tasks.previous_blocker: Small changes touched undocumented dependencies. Repeatable testing and release records were costly to establish for each reporting asset.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing development workspaces and deployment features provide the foundation. AI-assisted coding makes tailored comparison tests and metadata generators cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Novel transformations and disputed financial definitions still need skilled work. Tests cannot prove that a measure answers the right business question.
tasks.human_edge: Judge the business meaning of a change, diagnose unfamiliar failures, and decide whether evidence is sufficient for release.
tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time assessing proposed changes and less time repeating comparisons and documentation. They can recommend release readiness; financial definitions and production deployment retain their existing approvers.

reach.task: Test the reliability of financial reporting controls.
reach.learn: Control objectives, evidence retention, materiality, and segregation of duties.

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI can assist report and measure authoring, but this does not establish autonomous maintenance or safe deployment.
Databricks documents trusted assets and example queries for governed analytical answers, supporting investment in maintained definitions.
Versioned changes, regression comparisons, deployment gates, and generated change records can use deterministic technology. Savings and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: The first build covers one maintained reporting domain with development and production separation.
Routine parameter and layout edits are common enough to justify reusable configuration.
Bespoke query and model design remains human work; a general autonomous coding agent is unnecessary.
The BI lead is a distinct reviewer where staffing permits; another authorised reviewer can fill this role.
Build ranges include access and applicable national consultation work, but exclude unpredictable waiting periods.
GDPR access restrictions and EU AI Act literacy obligations apply where relevant; automated tests do not replace them.
unknowns: Are definitions, dependencies, source schemas, and reference results recorded?
What proportion of changes are routine configuration versus new analytical logic?
Which development, deployment, and rollback features are available?
Which changes affect personal data, employee monitoring, or regulated decisions?
research_questions: Which native configuration and deployment features remove the need for custom code?
Can historical defects be detected by proposed financial and access tests?
Which metadata fields are sufficient to generate useful change records without a model?
new_work: Maintain reference results and investigate legitimate differences.
Update tests when business definitions change.
Review deployment evidence and rehearse rollback.
Keep dependency metadata and generated guidance accurate.
tasks.statement: Maintain or update business intelligence tools, databases, dashboards, systems, or methods.

tasks.short: Deliver current intelligence to authorised users on time and resolve missing or delayed information.

steps.what: Maintain audience lists, reporting deadlines, and access requirements.
Check refresh status, reporting periods, and readiness before each delivery.
Chase missing source updates and warn owners about delivery risks.
Prepare separate report copies and attachments for different internal recipient groups.
Publish updates and manage report subscriptions for internal users.
Agree alternatives with users when information is late, incomplete, or unusually sensitive.

tasks.design: Configure subscriptions and access-controlled report links in the {BI}, replacing duplicate internal attachments. A deterministic flow in the {WORKFLOW} checks refresh and reconciliation status, holds unready deliveries, and sends bounded reminders through the {EMAIL} or {CHAT}. A small register records deadlines, recipients, source owners, and delivery exceptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Delivery depended on informal recipient lists and personal knowledge of source deadlines. Refresh success did not necessarily mean the figures were ready.
tasks.enabler_now: Native subscriptions cover routine distribution. Small deterministic integrations can connect readiness checks, ownership records, reminders, and delivery logs.
tasks.still_hard: Late sources, disputed deadlines, access changes, and urgent requests need negotiation. Removing attachments depends on users accepting governed links.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate what users can safely decide with incomplete information and communicate uncertainty without creating false confidence.

ambition.what: Weekly cash-position briefing for departmental budget holders

tasks.altitude: The analyst handles delivery exceptions and coaches users instead of checking every send. They can offer additional briefings within approved access limits; they gain no unilateral right to disclose confidential data.

reach.task: Coordinate timely cash-position information.
reach.learn: Cash cutoffs, bank reconciliation status, and the difference between available cash and accounting balances.

evidence.claim: Scheduled refresh and subscriptions are established ways to distribute recurring BI reports without a model.
Readiness rules, access-controlled links, bounded reminders, and delivery registers can be built deterministically. Build ranges are estimates.
The digest identifies Dutch works-council consent requirements relevant to systems monitoring individual staff performance; this is not a rule for every financial dashboard.

assumptions: This task covers internal distribution; external releases use the report-production task's release gate.
Access-controlled views can replace most internal attachments, while mandatory snapshots remain available.
The readiness rule requires successful controls and the correct reporting period, not merely a completed refresh.
The mailbox share is above the weak prior because this baseline includes substantial source chasing.
Shared delivery steps also appear in report production; savings across tasks must be deduplicated.
GDPR applies to personal data. Consultation requirements depend on national rules and the actual monitoring purpose.
Consent and access ranges include applicable consultation effort; formal waiting periods may extend elapsed delivery.
unknowns: Which deliveries already use subscriptions rather than manual sends?
Which audiences require immutable snapshots or offline access?
Who may approve recipient access and changed reporting deadlines?
Are source readiness and ownership available as structured records?
Does any report expose individual employee performance?
research_questions: Can native subscriptions enforce the required readiness conditions?
Which users can move from attachments to links without losing necessary functionality?
What reminder limits and escalation timings avoid repeated noise?
new_work: Review failed deliveries and unresolved source delays.
Maintain recipient access, source ownership, and reporting calendars.
Adjust readiness rules after process changes.
Remove obsolete subscriptions and duplicate audience views.
tasks.statement: Manage timely flow of business intelligence information to users.

tasks.short: Identify industry and regional trends and explain their implications for financial planning.

steps.what: Agree the business question, comparison markets and planning horizon.
Retrieve market observations and internal revenue data.
Align periods, currencies and regional classifications in a comparison workbook.
Compare trends, segments and historical benchmarks to shortlist material changes.
Write a trend brief with charts, explanations and possible financial implications.

loop.input: Reviewed trend shortlist, computed comparisons, source references and analysis scope.
loop.output: Draft trend brief distinguishing observed changes, hypotheses and evidence gaps.
loop.check: Validate every number against computed comparisons; require source references and analyst review of interpretations.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unsupported explanations remain flagged for the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply charts and figures, but explanations need context and qualified prose.

steps.what: Assess implications and approve recommendations for planning.
Circulate the approved recommendation to agreed recipients.

tasks.design: Configured feeds load approved observations into the {DATA_PLATFORM}; deterministic transformations align periods and classifications, and the {BI} highlights material changes. A template generator adds charts and a bounded writing loop drafts the brief in the {DOCS}; the analyst reviews the explanation and the financial manager approves recommendations before configured distribution through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source definitions and reporting periods differed, while recurring analysis logic lived in workbooks. Writing explanations required business context that fixed templates could not capture.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors, semantic models and subscriptions cover much of the pipeline. AI-assisted development lowers the effort of building mappings and validation; a bounded writing loop can use verified figures.
tasks.still_hard: Sparse regional coverage, revised source series and misleading correlations remain. Strategic implications depend on commercial knowledge and cannot be inferred safely from trend strength alone.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst distinguishes a meaningful market shift from a reporting change and tests explanations with people who understand the business.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of regions requiring revised revenue scenarios.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time rebuilding comparisons and more time testing explanations. They can initiate scenario reviews within agreed materiality thresholds; financial managers retain planning approval.

reach.task: Translate regional demand changes into revenue scenarios.
reach.learn: Revenue-driver bridges, forecast sensitivities and how uncertainty enters a financial plan.

evidence.claim: Prepared semantic models support assisted report creation, but model preparation affects reliability.
Period alignment, currency conversion, threshold checks and scheduled comparisons can use deterministic pipelines.
The proposed build ranges are planning estimates, not measured delivery times or guaranteed savings.

assumptions: The initial scope covers one market dataset, internal revenue data and an existing reporting environment.
Collection is handled by the separate source-collection task; this task starts with released observations.
The mostly structured-input prior fits the calculations, but interpretation remains substantial despite the automation classification.
GDPR applies where personal data is used; the EU AI Act applies according to intended use. The initial scope excludes individual creditworthiness and employment decisions.
unknowns: Available regional coverage, source revision policies and licensing permissions.
Whether configured connectors already expose the required revenue and market data.
Who can authorise scenario reviews and which materiality thresholds they use.
research_questions: Which historical trend flags would have changed a planning decision?
How well do simple seasonal comparisons perform against the analyst's current shortlist?
new_work: Review generated explanations and investigate unsupported causal claims.
Maintain classification mappings, thresholds and reference-rate policies.
Monitor source revisions and assess whether earlier recommendations need correction.
Maintain approved distribution lists and access permissions.
tasks.statement: Identify and analyze industry or geographic trends with business strategy implications.

tasks.short: Document agreed requirements, definitions and acceptance criteria for finance reports and dashboards.

steps.what: Collect report requests, examples and requested changes.
Clarify decisions, audiences, measures and acceptance criteria with the requester.
Map requested measures to source fields, definitions and access constraints.
Write the specification, including calculations, layouts, refresh rules and acceptance tests.

loop.input: Requirements notes, approved metric references, source mapping and specification template.
loop.output: Draft specification with traceable requirements, proposed acceptance tests and explicit unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate referenced fields and metric identifiers; mark new calculations as proposals and require approval before delivery.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unresolved requirements enter the clarification queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: The template is deterministic, but free-text requests need interpretation and readable acceptance criteria.

steps.what: Review definitions, resolve open questions and approve the report specification.
Retype approved specification details into the delivery ticket.
Send the approved specification link to the delivery team.

tasks.design: A configured intake form in the {PROJECT} captures requests and links them to definitions from the {BI} and {DATA_PLATFORM}. A template generator and bounded drafting loop create the specification in the {DOCS}; approval advances the original request into delivery, removes duplicate entry and triggers a notification through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements arrived in inconsistent language, definitions were scattered and delivery records duplicated approved documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured intake, linked records and metadata checks are established capabilities. A small drafting loop can turn notes into a consistent specification while exposing unanswered questions.
tasks.still_hard: Stakeholders may disagree about what a measure means or which decision the report supports. Documentation cannot settle those disagreements or repair absent source data.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst makes ambiguous requests testable and brings conflicting definitions into an explicit agreement.
tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more of the week resolving metric disagreements and less copying specifications. Approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Specify reconciliation criteria for management reports.
reach.learn: Ledger control totals, posting periods, adjustments and the distinction between management and statutory measures.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, document templates and linked delivery records can remove duplicate specification entry.
A bounded drafting loop can propose specifications from notes, with field validation and human approval before implementation.
The build ranges are estimates for a narrow specification workflow, not documented implementation results.

assumptions: The scope covers one finance reporting team and one specification template.
An existing data catalogue and metric definitions can be referenced, even if incomplete.
Although the inputs concern structured systems, request wording and agreement on meaning still require interpretation.
Specifications record GDPR access and retention requirements where personal data is involved, and EU AI Act requirements where applicable.
Employee-level reporting requirements may require consultation under national rules; the estimate assumes no new employee-monitoring purpose.
unknowns: Whether the current delivery record can reference the approved specification without duplicating its contents.
Who has authority to approve metric definitions and report acceptance criteria.
Whether national rules require consultation for any proposed reporting purpose.
research_questions: Which missing specification fields most often cause delivery rework?
Can existing definitions populate most of the template without model involvement?
new_work: Review proposed acceptance criteria and resolve flagged ambiguities.
Maintain templates, required fields and links to metric definitions.
Check that specification versions remain linked to the correct delivery record.
Monitor drafting failures and revise the bounded prompt and validation rules.
tasks.statement: Document specifications for business intelligence or information technology reports, dashboards, or other outputs.

tasks.short: Explain changes to reports, tools and metric definitions to their users.

steps.what: Collect released changes from the {PROJECT}, {BI} and {DOCS}.
Identify affected users and communication priority from the report catalogue.
Write explanations, examples and migration instructions in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved release facts, metric definitions, affected audiences and a guidance template.
loop.output: Report-change guidance linked to release facts.
loop.check: Check identifiers, dates and links automatically; the analyst approves accuracy and user impact.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per release; missing facts return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle routine notices; explaining varied metric changes needs short, audience-specific prose.

steps.what: Publish guidance in the {DOCS} and notify users through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}.
Discuss confusing changes and collect user feedback.

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} builds an enhancement register from approved releases in the {PROJECT} and report metadata in the {BI}. A recipient map and templates handle routine notices; a bounded drafting loop prepares complex guidance for analyst approval in the {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} publishes approved guidance and sends targeted notifications through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Release facts, report ownership and guidance were maintained separately. Keeping audience mappings current often cost more than sending a broad notice.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing release records, subscriptions and interfaces support most of the flow. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort; a small drafting loop handles varied explanations.
tasks.still_hard: Dependencies and report ownership can be incomplete. Users need human explanations when changes affect established decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise which changes will confuse users and explain their practical consequences.

ambition.what: Report-change impact previews for budget holders before major metric changes.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time assembling and sending notices and more time helping users adopt changes. Publishing authority stays within the existing release policy; no new financial decision rights arise.

reach.task: Explain how changed metric definitions affect budget variance interpretation.
reach.learn: Budget ownership, variance conventions and planning deadlines.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-8; 10-30 if employee consultation is required under national rules

evidence.claim: Release-triggered templates, recipient mappings and internal notifications can use deterministic automation.
Typical steps, time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.

tasks.short: Build finance data models, transformations and dashboards from approved reporting requirements.

Design data grain, joins, historical treatment and measure semantics.
Implement transformations, incremental loads and data-quality checks.
Implement model relationships, measures and access roles.
Assemble dashboard pages, filters and navigation.
Reconcile dashboard totals and test filters against ledger exports and expected results.
Validate business behaviour and accept the dashboard for release.
Publish the dashboard and apply approved production access.

tasks.design: Reusable generators turn approved definitions into deterministic transformations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} and model components in the {BI}; existing dashboard templates supply standard pages. Automated reconciliation and access tests produce a validation report, while business acceptance and a production release gate control publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every dashboard repeated schema inspection, transformation coding, measure setup and manual reconciliation. Bespoke source structures and weak reusable templates made the setup cost high.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted development makes deterministic generators and adapters cheaper to build, while existing deployment and testing capabilities provide controlled reuse. No runtime model or autonomous agent is required for this scoped solution.
tasks.still_hard: Source semantics, historic restatements, many-to-many joins and access boundaries need experienced design. Standard templates cover less of a genuinely novel analytical application.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst chooses a model that preserves business meaning and recognises when a plausible total hides a wrong join or definition.

Judge discrepancies and record defects or justified differences in the {PROJECT}.
Approve business acceptance or return the report for correction.

tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were expressed inconsistently, and test evidence was assembled separately from financial reconciliations. Automated checks could verify calculations without establishing business usefulness.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable criterion types, query interfaces and versioned datasets make repeatable checks practical. AI-assisted coding makes the test harness cheaper to build without putting a model in the calculation path.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous requirements, historical restatements and valid accounting differences need interpretation. Visual usability and whether a report supports the intended decision still require people.
tasks.human_edge: Define meaningful acceptance criteria and distinguish a defect from a legitimate business difference.

tasks.altitude: The analyst runs fewer repetitive checks and spends more time designing useful tests and resolving discrepancies. Business acceptance remains with the finance manager; the analyst gains no release authority automatically.

tasks.short: Collect, standardise and release market intelligence from public, licensed and internal field sources.

Download datasets from public statistics portals and licensed data portals.
Gather field reports and approved source attachments from the shared mailbox.
Read reports and extract relevant indicators with their source references.

loop.input: Approved source documents and a fixed schema for indicators, periods, geography, units and source spans.
loop.output: Candidate observations with quoted evidence and explicit missing fields.
loop.check: Match numeric values to cited source spans; validate dates, units and required fields; analyst approves admission.
loop.stop: Two attempts per document and at most 30 supplied pages; ambiguous or oversized documents enter manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Document layouts and narrative field reports vary; fixed parsers remain the first choice for stable formats.

steps.what: Standardise structured feeds and extracted observations into common periods, units and classifications.
Check completeness, duplicates and revisions, then approve the dataset.
Publish the approved dataset and its source metadata.
Notify authorised users that the dataset is ready.

tasks.design: A source register in the {WORKFLOW} drives scheduled adapters from public statistics services in the {OTHER}, licensed feeds in the {PARTNER_PORTAL} and approved attachments in the {EMAIL}. Fixed parsers handle stable formats, a bounded extraction loop handles variable documents, and deterministic checks on the {DATA_PLATFORM} prepare a versioned dataset for analyst approval and release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources mixed downloads, documents and mailbox attachments, with inconsistent units and release calendars. Maintaining individual adapters often cost more than repeating manual collection.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable adapters and validation libraries reduce repeated engineering. Bounded extraction can handle variable documents while preserving source evidence and leaving uncertainty visible.
tasks.still_hard: Licences may restrict storage or redistribution, portals change and source revisions can invalidate earlier comparisons. Missing coverage cannot be solved by extraction or silently filled.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst chooses credible sources and recognises when apparently comparable indicators measure different things.

ambition.what: A versioned market-indicator feed with source lineage for budget analysts.

tasks.short: Analyze technology trends and commercial data to recommend markets for product development or sales growth.

steps.what: Agree market questions, comparison periods and commercial success criteria.
Retrieve sales, margin and market series from {BI}, {CRM} and {ERP}.
Read {OTHER} research feeds and save cited technology extracts in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Licensed technology publications, analysis scope and extraction schema.
loop.output: Dated claims, technology categories, source passages and source references.
loop.check: Require a matching source passage for each claim; analyst reviews relevance and unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per publication; unreadable or unsupported material goes to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Dates and identifiers follow rules, but technology claims appear in varied prose.

steps.what: Align market categories, currencies and periods in {SPREADSHEET}; reconcile totals.
Compare growth, adoption and margins in {BI}; identify credible signals and limitations.
Assess market attractiveness, strategic fit and alternative explanations.
Draft the market brief in {DOCS}, linking recommendations to charts and sources.

loop.input: Analyst recommendation, approved findings, source references and brief template.
loop.output: Draft market brief with evidence links and explicit assumptions.
loop.check: Insert figures deterministically; verify references; analyst checks interpretation and removes unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved passages remain flagged for manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble charts, but explaining different technology signals requires limited prose drafting.

steps.what: Challenge recommendations, approve the brief and select follow-up investigations.

tasks.design: Configure scheduled extracts from {CRM}, {ERP} and {BI}; deterministic jobs on {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile periods, currencies and market mappings before refreshing {BI}. A bounded extraction loop builds a cited evidence register in {DOCS}, while a separate drafting loop combines approved findings with the analyst's recommendation. Record investigation decisions in {PROJECT} after the finance manager approves the brief.
tasks.previous_blocker: Commercial data and technology evidence used different categories and refresh cycles. Reusable reconciliation rules and reliable source links required substantial setup.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors and scheduled reporting handle much of the data flow. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort, while bounded models can extract and draft prose; neither removes the need for sound market definitions.
tasks.still_hard: Market coverage is uneven, adoption measures lag and technology publicity can resemble demand. Strategic fit and commercial causality remain judgement calls.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge whether a visible trend creates profitable demand, identify missing evidence and choose a useful market experiment.

ambition.what: Market experiment scorecards linking technology signals to testable adoption and margin assumptions.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time assembling extracts and briefs, and more time testing commercial assumptions. They gain discretion to prioritise follow-up investigations within an agreed scope; investment approval stays with the finance manager.

tasks.still_hard: Causal explanations, changing market conditions and political or operational constraints remain difficult. Faster analysis cannot resolve missing evidence.
